citations.assertion: Testator James Glasgow Senior; reviewed family role. James Glasgow Senior’s original Davidson County will is now located in volume 7, printed pages 407–408, FamilySearch images 233–234. It expressly names a son James and appoints him an executor. The closing probate entry records that a son/executor James qualified in April 1820; the recording heading is June 1820. The will is dated November 1819; no exact day is adopted from this reading. This replaces the earlier original-uninspected status. It confirms the named-son role underlying James-2492’s existing 94% assessment, while identification of that son with the Smith County adult remains a separate inference. It does not name Wesley or prove James-2492 was Wesley’s father. The original contains other family and property clauses; this review publishes only the checked son/executor scope, without assigning untraced beneficiaries to modern profiles. Wesley-2476’s selected father James-2492 remains Possible at 35%; James-2492’s own father James-634 remains Confident at 94%. The census age slots are compatible household evidence, not named kin or independent birth entries. No new parent, exact vital date, maternal attachment, profile merger or confidence gain follows. The cited indexes and their newly inspected originals describe the same underlying events and are not independent witnesses.
